name: Tom Scott
hook: A jazz saxophonist who recorded his first album as a teenager, and whose solo became the horn line of 'T.R.O.Y.'.

blurb.age7: A saxophone player. A few notes from one of his songs became the most famous part of 'T.R.O.Y.'.
blurb.age13: Tom Scott is a saxophonist from Los Angeles. He recorded his first album, The Honeysuckle Breeze, for the jazz label Impulse! in 1967, when he was a teenager. One track, 'Today', is his version of a Jefferson Airplane song. In 1992 Pete Rock took parts of its saxophone solo and made them the main melody of 'They Reminisce Over You (T.R.O.Y.)'. Scott went on to a long career as a session and jazz-fusion player.
blurb.adult: Scott is on the map as a sample hub (Q21), and 'Today' shows how far a sample can travel: a rock song, covered as easy-listening jazz, then cut into a hip-hop memorial for a dead friend.
